title: Tool calling bridge and contract mapper for OpenAI-style tools vs legacy functions
creator: Priya Nair
description: Design and implement a runtime bridge that maps OpenAI-style tool calling (name/parameters/schema + streaming tool outputs) to our legacy function invocation surface used by older customers and internal backends. The goal is to provide a transparent compatibility layer so hosted and dedicated tenants can adopt OpenAI-style tool contracts without breaking existing integrations or runtime optimizations (batching, KV cache, streaming).
acceptance_criteria: 1) OpenAI tool call payloads (tool name, param schema, call hints) are deterministically mapped to legacy function identifiers with a reversible mapping. 2) Streaming partial tool outputs are relayed to client SDKs in the new tool-event envelope and also delivered to legacy function consumers as buffered/committed events. 3) Parameter and response schemas are validated and automatically transformed for common mismatches (snake_case vs camelCase, typed enums, nested structs) with configurable strict/lenient modes. 4) Controlled name-collision policy implemented (namespace + suffix strategy) and documented. 5) End-to-end tests (unit, integration, e2e with runtime) and canary rollout plan are present in the PR. 6) Backward-compatible error shapes and retry semantics documented and returned for both OpenAI-style and legacy clients.
technical_decisions: - Mapping: tool.name -> legacy_function_id via hashing + deterministic prefix (eg. tool:translate -> legacy:tf-translate-<shorthash>). This ensures stable ids even as display names change. - Naming policy: prefer namespace user.toolname; for collisions append _vN where N increments. - Schema translation: implement a small declarative rule engine (yaml-based) that converts parameter keys and types. Defaults: camelCase->snake_case and basic enum coercion. - Streaming model: runtime emits tool-stream-chunk events; bridge buffers micro-batches to legacy functions that expect chunked frames and exposes commit/finalize events. Clients see partial tokens in OpenAI-style stream frames. - Transactional semantics: introduce optimistic-commit header for multi-tool transactions; support compensating calls in legacy paths for rollback. - ABI versioning: add header X-Tool-Bridge-Version and schema_version to tool metadata to allow graceful upgrades. - Error mapping: map 4xx/5xx from legacy to standard tool_error codes; expose diagnostic metadata in structured output while masking PII. - Performance: keep per-token latency delta < 10ms for lightweight translation rules; expensive rule sets run in async transformers with fallbacks.
implementation_plan: 1) Design RFC and API contract (Confluence) -> 2025-02-18. 2) Prototype adapter in runtime gateway that handles name mapping and basic schema translation -> 2025-02-25. 3) Add streaming relay with commit/finalize semantics and end-to-end test harness -> 2025-03-05. 4) Implement declarative rule engine for common schema transforms -> 2025-03-10. 5) Security review and QA (fuzzing for schema converters, dependency checks) -> 2025-03-12. 6) Canary rollout on a small host group with opt-in feature flag -> 2025-03-18. 7) Full rollout and docs (SDK examples, migration guide) -> 2025-04-01.
risks: - Name collisions across tenant-provided tool names could cause silent behavior changes if mapping is not reversible. Mitigation: deterministic mapping + visible alias table per tenant. - Complex schema transforms may be slow or lossy for deeply nested objects; mitigation: opt-in strict mode that rejects untranslatable payloads and tooling to generate mappings. - Streaming contract mismatch might increase latency for legacy functions that expect larger frames; mitigation: adaptive batching and per-function policy knobs. - Security: malformed tool schemas could be used to exfiltrate data via crafted fields; mitigation: schema validation, content filtering, and KMS/HSM checks for sensitive fields. - Operational: rollout could surface regressions in autoscaling; mitigation: canary + autoscaling guardrails + feature flagging.
testing_plan: - Unit tests for name mapping and schema translation rules. - Integration tests: runtime gateway -> bridge -> legacy function adapter with simulated streaming. - E2E: SDK-level tests (Python/Node) that exercise partial streaming, finalize, and error paths. - Load tests to measure latency overhead with typical token sizes. - Regression suite covering previously supported legacy function behaviors. - Golden example suite: 20 canonical tool contracts + corresponding legacy function fixtures.
